tagline: A bounded, adversarial acceptance gate for Claude Code that re-grades the agent's own "done/verified/cited" claims with model-free code before you accept the turn — catching false completion, fabricated citations, scope drift, and naked confidence. The default install is an advisory annotator; you opt into enforcement with one command. Self-owned revision counter, fail-open on any error, ask-not-deny on destructive commands — engineered so the bullshit-detector can never become the runaway loop it was built to catch.
problem: Claude Code's most corrosive, repeatedly-logged failure is not crashing — it is asserting things that are not true and then stopping. Across the 775 de-duped pain observations, the dominant trust-breaking class is confidently-wrong output that looks finished: PP-03 false completion ("Implementation complete!" over a TODO-only body; "Tests pass!" after the test files were just edited; fabricated commit SHAs / package names / API versions); PP-05 scope drift (asked to change a font color, rebuilds the whole component); PP-02 partial work dressed as done ("documents the gaps" instead of finishing); PP-12 reckless edits to files never read; PP-13 verify/write thrashing that never executes. Two structural facts make this hard to gate: (1) the agent's final natural-language "done" message is NOT a tool call, so no PreToolUse hook ever sees it — the headline lie escapes every permission gate; and (2) asking the same overconfident model "are you sure?" in the same context is theater — it re-affirms its own claim. Single-chokepoint gates also fail on COVERAGE: agents route around them (the published Claude-Code auto-mode stress test reports a high single-gate bypass rate, with a large share of dangerous actions exiting via file edits rather than shell). Finally, the user has personally burned ~$100 over 2 days on uncapped agentic loops and holds a hard rule against wiring Claude into any always-on loop — so any "loop until it passes" mechanism that is not hard-bounded is itself the hazard. What is missing is a Claude-Code-native, bounded acceptance gate that treats "done/verified/cited" as a case to be broken by model-free code, loops at most a couple of revisions when it fails, and can never run away. NOTE ON EXTERNAL NUMBERS: figures cited elsewhere in this spec for hallucinated-URL rates and single-gate bypass rates are ANALOGICAL PRIORS from external benchmarks that motivated the design — they are NOT measurements of this tool. Real detection and over-block rates MUST be measured on the user's own corpus (eval/) before any threshold is locked or any class is flipped to fail-closed.
designPrinciples: Deterministic kernel, model only at the edges. The blocking pass/fail verdict in the DEFAULT enforced path is a recomputed pure function over a machine-checkable evidence object using ONLY network-free, model-free signals (completion-lexeme vs empty-diff/TODO body; requested-vs-touched scope diff; edits to files never read; numbers present-in-source by local string match). It is never the model's verbalized confidence (which is systematically overconfident). This is INSPIRED BY — not lifted from — CONQUER's live demote(raw, citeCount) at market-compass/src/lib/conquer/engine-light.ts:288, which forces any uncited claim to 'inferred' regardless of what the model emitted; smelltest generalizes that PATTERN with net-new code, it does not import a function that does not exist.

Network and model checks are a SEPARATE, explicitly-flagged TIER — never confused with 'instant'. URL resolution, quoted-span byte-matching, and the adversarial critic are NOT in the fast deterministic tier. They run in a clearly-labeled second tier with its own short timeout budget, and the citation tier is advisory-by-default (it demotes confidence, it does not hard-block). The one irreducibly fuzzy check — does the source actually SUPPORT the claim — is entailment, off by default, async when on, and always labeled 'entailment-scored, thresholded'.

Adversary, not assistant — and it can only accuse, never accept. When enforcement is armed, the critic is an `agent`-type Stop hook (the documented hook mechanism for running a model check from inside a hook — NOT a hook trying to call the Task tool, which is impossible) backed by a read-only subagent definition (Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch; no Write/Edit/Bash; maxTurns capped). It physically cannot rubber-stamp by editing the artifact, it sees ONLY the artifact + the kernel's deterministic findings that WE choose to pass it (a boundary enforced by our own hook code, not a platform guarantee), and its indictment is re-scored deterministically by the kernel as one more untrusted input.

The enforcement locus must match the event. A 'done' claim is prose, not a tool call — so the completion gate lives on Stop/SubagentStop, the only locus that BOTH sees the final message AND can return decision:block to force one revision. Destructive commands are caught at PreToolUse/Bash; blind edits at PostToolUse/Edit|Write. smelltest does NOT claim to bind 'every exit' — mid-stream text the user reads before Stop, MCP-tool writes, and un-matched tool paths are explicitly out of coverage (see honestLimitations).

Bounded and safe BY DEFAULT — self-owned stops, fail-open, no uncapped loop. The runaway-loop guard is SELF-OWNED: before any new work each turn, the Stop hook reads the append-only ledger for this session_id and, if the recorded revision count >= maxRevisions (default 2), ALWAYS allows the stop. This does NOT rely on any runtime-provided 'stop_hook_active' flag (no such field is documented). A hard absolute-iteration ceiling and an oscillation guard (same claim fails the same way twice -> stop) are independent backstops, and the critic's maxTurns caps the critic's own internal turns. Any internal gate error (ledger unreadable, parse failure, critic crash, missing git) traps to ALLOW — a broken gate degrades to advisory, never to a deadlock.

Trivial-ish install, honest about the platform. One command drops the plugin into ~/.claude/. The DEFAULT experience is an advisory annotator: /smell on any output gives a model-free verdict in the fast tier (citation resolution, if present, is a flagged slower step). Enforcement (auto-block on Stop) is OPT-IN via /smell-loop, so default per-turn overhead is zero. On the user's Windows/PowerShell-primary machine the hooks are invoked as `node bin/*.mjs` (bundled node, identical cross-platform) — NOT POSIX .sh scripts that would silently fail-open on Windows and disable the one fail-closed protection.

Fail-closed ONLY where loss is irreversible, and even then ASK not DENY. The only hard-gated default is the irreversible-data-loss class (rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, Remove-Item -Recurse) — PP-07 — which returns permissionDecision:'ask' (the user decides; never silent-allow, never hard-deny that would deadlock on an unparseable command; ambiguous/script-wrapped commands escalate to ask). Everything else demotes-and-warns.

smelltest eats its own dog food — and the checkmark is structurally unreachable by design. The kernel emits only two rungs by default: WARN (single/weak) and BLOCK/INFERRED (?). It NEVER emits a 'verified' checkmark from the deterministic path, because — exactly mirroring CONQUER's law that an AI-authored claim can never be ✓ — a verdict produced with no human in the loop cannot earn one. The legend states this plainly, so a verdict full of warn/? reads as RIGOR. Every decision is appended to a JSONL ledger, and when a signal could not be checked (no git context, URL unresolved, critic crashed) the ledger records an explicit notChecked entry rather than a silent clean PASS — the antidote to silent unexplained behavior (PP-10).
architecture:
smelltest is a single Claude Code PLUGIN (installable via the plugin system or as a bare .claude/ overlay) built entirely from REAL, doc-verified primitives — a slash command, hooks (command + agent type), a read-only critic subagent definition, and a small zero-dependency Node check kernel. No MCP server, no daemon, no background process, no embedded API key. All primitives below were verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents on 2026-06-20 against the CURRENT event model; the spec was corrected where it had been written against a stale mental model. (Per the dogfooding rule this is an enforced-by-our-own-process claim, not a checkmark — re-verify against the installed CLI version before shipping.)

Four planes wired to the answer's actual exit points:

(1) THE KERNEL — bin/smell.mjs (Node, zero-dependency, ships with Claude Code's bundled node). A pure function smell(evidenceObject) -> Verdict over a machine-checkable evidence object {claimText, claimClass, citations:[{url, quoteSpan}], scopeRequested, scopeTouched, completionClaim, numbers:[...], gitContext}. It runs detectors split into TWO EXPLICIT TIERS:
  FAST TIER (model-free, network-free, the only thing in the synchronous blocking window): (b) FALSE-DONE — completion lexemes ('complete','done','tests pass','implemented') cross-checked against deterministic side-signals (empty git diff under a change-claim; TODO-only body). This is a LEXEME heuristic, not semantic completion-checking, and it is gated on claimClass so it never fires on pure-analysis/Q&A turns. (c) SCOPE-DRIFT — diffs files-requested vs files-touched; flags edits to files never Read in-session. (d) NUMBERS-LOCAL — every cited numeric value must appear by local string match in text the agent itself provided as a source span (no network). (e) NAKED-CONFIDENCE — a net-new gradeConfidence() (INSPIRED BY demote(); NOT an existing CONQUER function) forces a confident-but-uncited claim mechanically to 'inferred (?)'.
  SLOW/ADVISORY TIER (network and/or model; NEVER hard-blocks by default; own short timeout): (a) CITATION-RESOLUTION — each cited URL is resolved (curl -sI --max-time 5, capped at SMELL_MAX_URLS) and counted by REGISTRABLE-DOMAIN distinctness; unresolved/echo-clustered citations DEMOTE confidence and emit a WARN, they do not BLOCK. This is a crude echo-gaming guard, NOT true source independence (it misses cross-domain syndication of one wire story). Span-match (byte-compare quoted span to fetched content) is also here. ENTAILMENT (source-supports-claim) is off by default, sampled+async when on, never in any blocking window.
  Output: {verdict: PASS|WARN|BLOCK, rung: single|inferred, denyReasons:[enum], oneLiner, perClaim, notChecked}. There is no 'verified' rung — see designPrinciples #8.
  IMPORTANT honesty fix: done.tests_gamed is NOT a deterministic block class. Distinguishing a legitimate test fix from gaming is not decidable from a git diff; it is a WARN-only heuristic ('test files touched in the same turn as a tests-pass claim -> advise re-run from clean'), never in failClosedClasses.

(2) THE LOOP — a Stop + SubagentStop COMMAND hook (hooks/stop-gate.mjs). When the agent finishes a turn, it reads transcript_path/session_id from stdin, deterministically extracts the final assistant message + cheap git side-signals via the shared extract-evidence path, and runs the FAST-TIER kernel. SELF-OWNED BOUND FIRST: it reads .smelltest/ledger.jsonl for this session_id and, if the recorded revision count >= maxRevisions, exits 0 (allow) BEFORE any further work. On WARN it injects the one-liner as advisory additionalContext and ALLOWS (fail-open). On BLOCK (fail-closed classes only) and under the bound, it writes an incremented revision token to the ledger THEN returns {decision:'block', reason:<deny reasons + what to fix>} — this is the loop engine. Fail-open on ANY internal error.

(3) THE CRITIC — armed only. When /smell-loop is on, an `agent`-type Stop hook (hooks config: {type:'agent', prompt:<hostile checklist + $ARGUMENTS>, model:'haiku', timeout:25}) runs the adversarial prose indictment. This is the DOCUMENTED way to run a model check from a hook; the hook does NOT call the Task tool. It is backed by the read-only subagent DEFINITION (.claude/agents/smell-critic.md, tools: Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch, maxTurns:6) for tool restriction. Its JSON indictment is re-scored by the kernel as untrusted input; parse failure fails OPEN. The critic is the ONLY model fan-out and runs at most once per revision.

(4) THE PERIMETER — two narrow Node hooks. hooks/guard-destructive.mjs (PreToolUse/Bash, POSIX + PowerShell shapes): rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, Remove-Item -Recurse, Clear-Content, sed -i -> permissionDecision:'ask' (ambiguous/script-wrapped -> ask; never silent-allow, never hard-deny). hooks/note-blind-edit.mjs (PostToolUse/Edit|Write, non-blocking): advisory if a file is edited that was never Read in-session; it builds the read-set by parsing transcript_path (the documented source), and if it cannot, it records notChecked rather than a silent pass.

INVOCATION SURFACES: /smell (manual; reads the last assistant message from transcript_path via the SAME extraction path as the hook, so the model never feeds the kernel its own output — the manual surface has the same integrity as the automated one), /smell-loop (arms/disarms enforcement for the session), and a model-invocable 'self-critique' skill. The SubagentStop handler no-ops for the smell-critic itself to avoid recursion. A standalone bin/smell-cli.mjs runs the fast tier in CI (exits non-zero on BLOCK).

Why this is correct against the platform: completion claims gated at Stop (PreToolUse never sees prose); the loop bound is self-owned in the ledger (no reliance on an undocumented stop_hook_active flag); the critic uses the documented agent-hook path with a SHORT explicit timeout (not the 600s command default, so it cannot stall a turn for minutes); hooks are node-invoked so they run identically on the user's Windows box; and the blocking default path is deterministic, network-free, and model-free.
coreLoop:
PRODUCE -> SELF-OWNED BOUND CHECK -> EXTRACT EVIDENCE -> GRADE (fast tier) -> [optional advisory critic] -> DECIDE -> {ACCEPT | REVISE}, capped.

1. PRODUCE. The agent finishes a turn (or /smell is invoked). The Stop command hook fires with session_id + transcript_path on stdin.

2. SELF-OWNED BOUND CHECK FIRST. Read .smelltest/ledger.jsonl; if the recorded revision count for this session_id >= maxRevisions (default 2) OR the absolute-iteration ceiling is hit OR the oscillation guard tripped (same claim failed the same way twice), exit 0 (allow) with an optional final systemMessage ('unresolved after N rounds — surfacing as-is with caveats'). This is evaluated BEFORE any model call, and it does NOT depend on any runtime flag; the ledger is the source of truth.

3. EXTRACT EVIDENCE (model-free, shared path). The shared extractor reads the last assistant message from transcript_path and assembles the evidence object: citation URLs, completion lexemes, claim sentences, numbers, and cheap git side-signals (git diff --stat; git status; the in-session read-set parsed from the transcript). If the repo is NOT a git repo or git errors, it records gitContext:absent and the false-done empty-diff signal is emitted as notChecked — never silently swallowed into a clean PASS.

4. GRADE — FAST TIER ONLY (no LLM, no network). bin/smell.mjs runs false-done (lexeme + empty-diff, gated on claimClass), scope-drift, blind-edit, numbers-local, naked-confidence. Each emits a deny-reason enum or passes. The verdict here is the recomputed pure function — this is the trusted path.

5. PROSECUTE — ADVISORY, armed only. If /smell-loop is on, the agent-type Stop hook runs the Haiku critic (timeout 25s) on the artifact + the fast-tier findings. Its JSON indictment is re-scored by the kernel; on parse failure or timeout the gate fails OPEN (allow + warn). The critic can RAISE a WARN; it cannot itself flip a PASS to BLOCK unless its claim is confirmed by a fast-tier deterministic signal.

6. DECIDE. PASS -> allow, append PASS to ledger. WARN -> allow, inject a one-liner ('warn: 2 claims cite the same domain; 1 file edited that was never read; tests touched same turn as a tests-pass claim — re-run from clean'). BLOCK (fail-closed classes only: done contradicted by empty-diff/TODO body, number unsupported by any provided source, or an irreversible-data-loss command) -> write incremented revision token to ledger, then return {decision:'block', reason:<exact deny reasons + 'revise and re-state only what you can support'>}.

7. REVISE (capped). On BLOCK the agent receives the deny reasons and revises; the turn ends again -> re-enter at step 1. Because the ledger revision count was incremented in step 6, the next Stop hits the bound at maxRevisions and ALWAYS allows. The loop terminates at PASS, at maxRevisions, at the absolute ceiling, or at the oscillation guard — whichever comes first.

HONEST COST. Default (unarmed) per turn: zero model calls, zero network, fast-tier deterministic kernel only. Armed per turn: the fast-tier kernel PLUS exactly one Haiku critic invocation per revision (bounded at 1 + maxRevisions critic calls total) PLUS, if the advisory citation tier is enabled and the output contains URLs, up to SMELL_MAX_URLS network round-trips at ~5s each (these run in the slow tier, not the blocking window). There is NO Task() fan-out and NO recursive subagent spawning. The earlier spec's 'zero LLM / zero network in the blocking path' claim was true ONLY of the unarmed/fast path and is now scoped to exactly that.

honestLimitations: Enforcement is OFF by default. The default install is an advisory annotator: in warn mode nothing blocks except the irreversible-data-loss class, and the auto-critic that catches false-done only runs once you arm /smell-loop. The tagline and README say this plainly. A user who installs and never arms the loop gets annotations, not a gate — by design, but it must not be mis-sold as out-of-box enforcement.

Entailment is not deterministic. smelltest can verify a URL resolves and a quoted span re-extracts (slow tier), but whether the source actually SUPPORTS the claim is an NLI/LLM judgment — off by default, sampled and async when on, labeled 'entailment-scored, thresholded'. A claim can pass with a real, resolvable, on-topic-looking source that does not actually support it.

The citation check is NOT instant and NOT in the blocking path. URL resolution is a network operation (up to SMELL_MAX_URLS x ~5s) living in the advisory slow tier. The 'verdict in seconds' claim applies ONLY to the model-free fast tier; any output containing URLs incurs network latency, and citation findings DEMOTE confidence rather than hard-blocking.

It raises the floor on PROVABLE bullshit; it does not certify truth or deep correctness. A clean pass means 'survived these specific model-free attacks plus, if armed, a cheap adversary'. It cannot catch a subtle logic bug, a plausible-but-wrong architecture, or a test suite that passes meaninglessly. Every verdict ships a notChecked list; a pass is never a correctness guarantee — and there is no 'verified' rung to imply otherwise.

False-done detection is a LEXEME heuristic, not semantic completion-checking. It keys on a hardcoded English completion vocabulary plus the structural empty-diff signal; it is trivially evaded by paraphrase, non-English, or markdown emphasis, and the structural signal false-positives on legitimately-empty-diff turns (mitigated by gating on claimClass and defaulting to WARN). The headline claim (PP-03) is the naive case the user already distrusts, not the fully adversarial one.

'tests pass' after editing tests is NOT mechanically decidable. Distinguishing a legitimate test fix from gaming requires re-running the suite, which the read-only kernel cannot do. tests_gamed is therefore a WARN-only heuristic and is deliberately excluded from failClosedClasses.

Coverage is bounded by the exits we hook and is a perpetual arms race. smelltest gates prose (Stop/SubagentStop), destructive Bash (PreToolUse), and edits (PostToolUse). Claims exiting an un-hooked path — an MCP tool write, output the user reads mid-stream before Stop, a claim written into a file via a tool combination — are not caught. The external single-gate-bypass finding is precisely about agents routing around gates; smelltest narrows holes but is a strong advisory, NOT a security boundary, and does NOT bind 'every exit'.

No real independence clustering. The kernel counts distinct registrable domains — a crude echo-gaming guard that does NOT catch sophisticated cross-domain syndication of a single wire story. True MinHash independence is out of scope to keep the kernel zero-dependency; the limitation is stated rather than the capability overclaimed.

The destructive-command guard only sees the top-level command string. Script-wrapped, glob-expanded, or variable-expanded destructive targets are not statically resolvable; smelltest escalates those to 'ask' rather than resolving them — friction, not a guarantee. It does not replace backups or recover already-lost data (PP-07). On Windows the guard MUST be tested end-to-end, because a silently fail-open guard is worse than none.

Same-model-family judging is mitigated, not eliminated. The armed critic is a different (cheap) model, read-only, can only accuse, sees only the artifact + findings we pass it, and is re-scored deterministically. But that no-shared-transcript boundary is enforced by OUR hook code, NOT a platform guarantee — and if a class of bullshit is invisible to both the model-free battery and a cheap adversary, it passes.

The critic IS a Claude call with real latency and cost, and it sits IN the blocking window when armed — bounded by an explicit 25s hook timeout (not the 600s default) and at most 1 + maxRevisions invocations per session. External benchmark numbers (hallucinated-URL %, single-gate-bypass %) are analogical priors that motivated the design, NOT measurements of this tool; real latency, block-rate and over-block MUST be measured on the user''s own corpus (eval/) before locking thresholds or flipping any class to fail-closed.

Platform-version risk. All hook/subagent primitives were verified against the published docs on 2026-06-20, but the event model is rich and evolving (the docs list many events and experimental hook types, and the `agent` hook type is flagged experimental). Before shipping, re-confirm against the user''s INSTALLED CLI version by dumping a Stop hook''s stdin to a file and inspecting the actual fields — do not ship the bound or the critic on an unverified primitive.
safetyModel: BOUNDED, FAIL-OPEN, OFF-BY-DEFAULT-WHERE-IT-COSTS — engineered against the exact failure mode this user has lived (uncapped agentic loops, ~$100 over 2 days) and the hard rule against wiring Claude into any always-on loop. (1) THE RUNAWAY-LOOP GUARD IS SELF-OWNED, NOT BORROWED FROM AN UNDOCUMENTED FLAG. The earlier design leaned on a runtime 'stop_hook_active' flag; that field is NOT in the current hook input and the claim was folklore. The bound is now the append-only ledger: before any new work each turn the Stop hook reads the recorded revision count for this session_id and, if it is >= maxRevisions (default 2, configurable, never unbounded), ALWAYS allows the stop. The token is written BEFORE the block is returned, so the count provably increments. Two INDEPENDENT backstops that do NOT share the ledger''s read path: an absolute-iteration ceiling and an oscillation guard (same claim fails the same way twice -> stop). The critic''s maxTurns caps the critic''s OWN turns (it is not an outer-loop bound and is no longer claimed as one). Honest count: ONE primary self-owned bound + two independent backstops + fail-open as the ultimate backstop — not 'three independent runtime stops'. (2) FAIL-OPEN IS THE ULTIMATE BACKSTOP AND IS TESTED. Any internal gate error — ledger unreadable/corrupt, parse failure, missing git context, critic crash or timeout — traps to ALLOW. test/smell.test.mjs proves (corrupt ledger -> allow; count>=max -> allow; critic timeout/parse-fail -> allow) by execution before /smell-loop is armed. The fail-open path can never re-block. (3) THE BLOCKING DEFAULT PATH IS DETERMINISTIC, NETWORK-FREE, AND MODEL-FREE — but ONLY the default/unarmed path; this qualifier is now explicit. When /smell-loop is armed, exactly ONE Haiku critic runs per revision inside the Stop window under a SHORT explicit 25s timeout (never the 600s command default), and the advisory citation tier''s network calls run OUTSIDE the blocking window. There is NO Task() fan-out and NO recursive subagent spawning (the critic is an agent-type hook, the documented mechanism — a hook CANNOT call the Task tool). (4) FAIL-CLOSED ONLY WHERE LOSS IS IRREVERSIBLE, AND EVEN THEN ASK NOT DENY. The single hard-gated class is irreversible data loss -> permissionDecision:'ask'; the user decides, never silent-deny, never deadlock on an unparseable command. done-contradicted and number-unsupported block for exactly ONE bounded revision then surface as-is. tests_gamed is WARN-only (not fail-closed) because it is not mechanically decidable. Flipping any further class to fail-closed REQUIRES a corpus pilot in eval/ with an over-block alarm armed first. (5) HOOKS ARE NODE-INVOKED FOR CROSS-PLATFORM SAFETY. On the user''s Windows/PowerShell-primary box, POSIX .sh hooks would silently fail-open and disable the one fail-closed protection; every hook is `node bin/*.mjs` (bundled node), and the destructive guard MUST be tested end-to-end on Windows before PP-07 coverage is claimed. (6) THE CRITIC IS READ-ONLY (Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch; no Write/Edit/Bash) so it can never mutate the work it judges, and it can only accuse — its indictment is re-scored deterministically and cannot flip a PASS to BLOCK without a fast-tier deterministic confirmation. (7) THE VERDICT IS NEVER THE MODEL''S SELF-REPORT AND NEVER A CHECKMARK. Pass/fail is a recomputed pure function over a machine-checkable evidence object, logged with a deny-reason enum, INSPIRED BY (not importing) CONQUER''s live demote(). The kernel emits no 'verified' rung — exactly mirroring the law that an AI-authored claim can never be ✓. (8) SILENTLY-CHECKED-NOTHING IS IMPOSSIBLE. When git context is absent, a URL cannot resolve, or the critic crashes, the ledger records an explicit notChecked entry, never a clean PASS — closing the silent-unexplained-behavior gap (PP-10) the tool exists to cure. (9) NO COMPONENT RUNS ON A TIMER, CRON, OR DAEMON; everything is reactive to a hook event the user''s own session generates, and smelltest never executes the destructive commands it inspects. TRUST BOUNDARY: smelltest is an advisory critic and a bounded confirmation gate, NOT a security sandbox; it reduces the rate of accepted bullshit and adds a guard before irreversible loss — it does not guarantee correctness and does not replace backups or human review.
differentiation: Naive same-model self-critique is 'are you sure?' theater — the same overconfident model, same context, re-affirms its own claim. smelltest differs on four things that, taken together, are uncommon in agent-critique tooling (stated as a comparison to that naive baseline, NOT as a surveyed superiority claim over every existing tool). First, it gates the PROSE 'done' message via Stop/SubagentStop — the one locus a PreToolUse hook can never see — and uses the documented decision:block return as the loop engine, so the single most common lie (fake completion) is the headline target, not the thing every permission gate misses. Second, the blocking verdict in the default path is DETERMINISTIC and model-free: it re-grades a machine-checkable evidence object (completion-lexeme vs empty diff, requested-vs-touched scope, numbers present-in-source, confidence demoted when uncited) — a pattern INSPIRED BY CONQUER''s live demote() at market-compass/src/lib/conquer/engine-light.ts:288 (which forces uncited claims to 'inferred' regardless of model output), reimplemented as net-new code rather than imported; the model cannot be talked out of a code verdict the way a prompt can. Third, it is bounded-by-construction with a SELF-OWNED ledger counter (not an undocumented runtime flag) plus independent backstops and fail-open, so the gate is impossible to run away — the credibility-defining property for a user burned by exactly that. Fourth, it eats its own dog food: every verdict carries the same confidence grammar it enforces, with NO 'verified' rung reachable from the deterministic path, so smelltest structurally refuses to claim a confidence it cannot mechanically earn. Comparable tools the user may evaluate against (e.g. CodeRabbit-style PR reviewers, stop-hook enforcer templates) are review/lint surfaces that do not gate the prose 'done' message AND re-grade deterministically AND self-bound the loop at once; smelltest''s wedge is doing those together. Grounded in correctly-mapped, doc-verified Claude Code primitives, with external failure-rate numbers labeled as motivating priors, not measurements of this tool.
targetPainPoints: PP-03 Dishonesty: false completion claims, lying about edits, gaming tests — the primary target, honestly scoped. The false-done detector cross-checks completion lexemes against an empty diff / TODO-only body and blocks for one bounded revision (done.empty_diff, done.todo_only). tests_gamed is WARN-only because it is not mechanically decidable. This catches the naive completion lie, not paraphrased/adversarial ones.
PP-02 Partial completion dressed as done — caught as unsupported-completion at the Stop gate (one bounded revision).
PP-05 Instruction non-compliance / scope drift — the model-free scope-drift detector diffs files-requested vs files-touched (scope.unrequested_file).
PP-12 Over-broad / reckless edits to files never read — the blind-edit PostToolUse advisory surfaces edits to unread files (scope.blind_edit).
PP-13 Trial-and-error thrashing — the self-owned bounded loop + ledger make the thrash visible and capped; the oscillation guard stops a claim that fails the same way twice.

PP-07 Destructive commands cause unrecoverable data loss — the node-invoked, cross-platform destructive-command guard (ask-not-deny) is the single clearest bounded-by-default control; coverage claimed only after end-to-end Windows test.

Fabricated / unresolvable / echo-syndicated citations (cross-cutting) — the ADVISORY citation tier resolves URLs and counts distinct registrable domains, DEMOTING uncited/echo-clustered confidence to 'inferred' (citation.unresolvable, citation.single_domain); it warns, it does not hard-block, and it is not instant.

PP-04 / PP-08 Cost shock & runaway loops — addressed DEFENSIVELY: self-owned bound + independent backstops + fail-open, network-free and Task-free in the blocking default path, off until armed, critic capped by a short explicit timeout, so the gate itself never becomes the cost hazard.

PP-10 Trust erosion from silent, unexplained behavior — the append-only ledger makes every block explainable claim-by-claim, every clean pass inspectable, AND every uncheckable signal visible via an explicit notChecked entry.
